## 94eda9b4c2fe

**Reproduced distribution hole / shortcut.** Generator SHA
`6410744c81f6cf274e9a2bcca64a327aa1e4119d2d847e01cb2d6719e404f60f`,
rule hash `8c96507ac166`.

The generator's `_TEMPLATES` support consists of exactly four normalized
3–4-cell shapes. Across 300 production draws (easy/medium/hard, seeds 0–99,
`sample_index = seed`), only those four shapes appeared and no unsupported shape
appeared. A canonical pair contains a lawful five-cell template with normalized
offsets `[(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)]`; the target's own `self_check` accepts
that counterexample.

A plausible shortcut—stamp only when the normalized source template is one of
the four generator templates, otherwise return an empty grid—is extensionally
identical on every possible current-generator template but differs on the
canonical five-cell input. The supported Racket rule stamps the five-cell shape;
the rival returns an empty grid.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/94eda9b4c2fe/finding.json` is self-contained;
`input.json`, `racket.json`, `rival.json`, `probe.json`, and
`apply-command.log` retain the components. The input belongs to the documented
canonical domain and passes the current validator (`counterexample_self_check:
[]`). This is a generator-domain restriction, not a claim that the Racket output
is wrong.

**Suggested owner repair.** Add the canonical five-cell template and at least one
additional lawful shape family, then declare a shape-support witness or test that
all canonical normalized templates are in generator support. A random 300-draw
diversity count alone cannot detect a closed four-template vocabulary.
